beliefs: Each character is mapped to chr(ord(ch)+1), then any resulting lowercase letter is uppercased, so a→B, b→C, y→Z, z→[ [E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6]
Uppercase letters, digits, space, and symbols are shifted by raw ASCII +1 with no further change (A→B, Z→[, 0→1, 9→:, space→!, ~→DEL) [E1, E2, E3, E5]
The uppercase step only affects characters whose ASCII+1 result is a lowercase letter, i.e. original lowercase a–y; z→{ is unaffected since '{' is not a letter [E2, E5, E6]
notes: Added an uppercasing pass after the +1 shift: lowercase inputs a–y become uppercase next letters, while z→{ and all non-lowercase inputs stay as raw ASCII+1. This matches all observed outputs including E6's 'Bc','Z{','B{'.
